subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept a broad operator-controlled host-local media/filesystem root policy for model-facing media reads, and if so should it be the shared tools.fs.roots design rather than a per-tool mediaLocalRoots field?
rationale: The requested behavior changes a host filesystem read boundary and overlaps an open broad PR; automation cannot choose the permanent security/config contract safely.

options.title: Adopt one shared root policy
options.body: Use tools.fs.roots or an equivalent shared schema across image/PDF/media/webchat/outbound paths, with explicit validation, docs, and upgrade/security tests.

options.title: Add a narrow media-only knob
options.body: Implement a smaller mediaLocalRoots field, but accept the maintenance risk of a separate trust boundary from other host-file policy paths.

options.title: Keep current scoped behavior
options.body: Do not add arbitrary host roots; users keep copying/symlinking files or rely only on channel-scoped inbound roots such as iMessage attachmentRoots.

recommendation.title: Adopt one shared root policy
recommendation.body: Use tools.fs.roots or an equivalent shared schema across image/PDF/media/webchat/outbound paths, with explicit validation, docs, and upgrade/security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the central local-root policy makes this the strongest code-history owner for the design choice.
